subject: math
title: Volume with Fractional Edge Lengths
seo_title: Grade 6 Volume Worksheets: Fractional Edge Lengths, V = l × w × h and V = B × h
standard_text: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = l w h and V = b h to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 volume worksheets with fractional edge lengths: pack boxes with 1/2-inch cubes, use V = l × w × h and V = B × h with fractions and mixed numbers, find a missing edge, and solve real-world word problems in cubic units. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: V = l × w × h works for fractions, too.
key_sub: A cube with 1/2-unit edges is 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8 cubic unit, so 8 of them fill 1 cubic unit. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply: 2 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 2 = 5/2 × 3/2 × 2 = 7 1/2.
body_html:
The big idea

Volume counts how many cubes fill a box. When an edge is a fraction, use small cubes that fit the fraction. A cube with 12-inch edges is 12 × 12 × 12 = 18 in³, because 8 of them fill a 1-inch cube.

Pack the box, then check with the formula

Count how many small cubes fit along each edge. Multiply to get the number of cubes. Then multiply by the volume of one small cube.

The formulas

V = l × w × h and V = B × h, where B is the area of the base. They work for fractions, too. Change mixed numbers to fractions, multiply the tops and the bottoms, then simplify.

Use V = B × h

The base of a box has an area of 7 12 in². The box is 1 12 in tall. What is its volume?

152 × 32 = 454 = 11 14.

Answer: 11 14 in³

Find a missing edge

A box has a volume of 5 58 ft³. It is 2 12 ft long and 1 12 ft wide. How tall is it?

B = 52 × 32 = 154 ft². h = 458 ÷ 154 = 458 × 415 = 180120 = 1 12.

Answer: 1 12 ft

Units

MeasureUnitExample
Length (1 edge)in, ft, cm, m2 12 ft
Area (a flat face, like the base)in², ft², cm², m²7 12 in²
Volume (space inside)in³, ft³, cm³, m³ (cubic inches, cubic feet …)10 ft³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the small cubes and stopping: 24 in³Each 12-inch cube is 18 in³: 24 × 18 = 3 in³
Adding the edges: 2 + 1 + 1 12 = 4 12Multiply all three: 2 × 1 × 1 12 = 3
2 12 × 3 12 = 6 14 (2 × 3, then 12 × 12)Change to 52 × 72 first: 354 = 8 34
Multiplying only two edgesThat is the area of the base. Multiply by the height, too
Writing in² for a volumeVolume is in cubic units: in³

faq.q: How do you find the volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths?
faq.a: Multiply length × width × height. Change mixed numbers to fractions first: 2 1/2 × 1 1/3 × 3 = 5/2 × 4/3 × 3 = 10 cubic units.

faq.q: Why is a cube with 1/2-inch edges equal to 1/8 cubic inch?
faq.a: Two of them fit along each edge of a 1-inch cube, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 of them fill it. Each one is 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8 cubic inch.

faq.q: What is the difference between V = l × w × h and V = B × h?
faq.a: They are the same formula. B is the area of the base (l × w), so B × h = l × w × h.

faq.q: How do you find a missing edge when you know the volume?
faq.a: Multiply the two known edges, then divide the volume by that product. For V = 5 5/8 ft³ with a 2 1/2 ft by 1 1/2 ft base, h = 5 5/8 ÷ 3 3/4 = 1 1/2 ft.

sets.title: Pack a box with small cubes

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 12-foot edges. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 3 ÷ 12 = 6, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3 cubes. 6 × 3 × 3 = 54 cubes. Each cube is 18 ft³, so V = 54 × 18 = 6 34 ft³. Check: 3 × 1 12 × 1 12 = 6 34.

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 13-foot edges. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 1 ÷ 13 = 3, 23 ÷ 13 = 2, 1 ÷ 13 = 3 cubes. 3 × 2 × 3 = 18 cubes. Each cube is 127 ft³, so V = 18 × 127 = 23 ft³. Check: 1 × 23 × 1 = 23.

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 13-inch edges. How many cubes fill the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 1 13 ÷ 13 = 4, 23 ÷ 13 = 2, 1 13 ÷ 13 = 4 cubes. 4 × 2 × 4 = 32 cubes. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 12-inch edges. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 2 12 ÷ 12 = 5, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3 cubes. 5 × 3 × 3 = 45 cubes. Each cube is 18 in³, so V = 45 × 18 = 5 58 in³. Check: 2 12 × 1 12 × 1 12 = 5 58.

items.q: A box is packed with 30 cubes that have 12-inch edges, with no gaps. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: One cube is 12 × 12 × 12 = 18 in³. 30 cubes: 30 × 18 = 308 = 3 34 in³.

items.q: How many cubes with 12-centimeter edges fill a box that is 3 cm long, 1 12 cm wide and 2 cm tall?
items.e: Along the edges: 6, 3 and 4 cubes (2 cubes for each centimeter). 6 × 3 × 4 = 72 cubes. Check: V = 9 cm³, and each cube is 18 cm³: 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: A wooden block is a cube with edges of 12 foot. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 12 × 12 × 12 = 18 ft³. Volume uses cubic units (ft³), not square units.

items.q: How many cubes with 12-inch edges fill a cube with 1-inch edges?
items.e: 2 small cubes fit along each edge: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. So each small cube is 18 in³.

items.q: How many cubes with 12-foot edges fill a box that is 2 12 ft long, 2 ft wide and 1 ft tall?
items.e: Along the edges: 5, 4 and 2 cubes (2 cubes for each foot). 5 × 4 × 2 = 40 cubes. Check: V = 5 ft³, and each cube is 18 ft³: 5 × 8 = 40.

items.q: A box is packed with 54 cubes that have 13-foot edges, with no gaps. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: One cube is 13 × 13 × 13 = 127 ft³. 54 cubes: 54 × 127 = 5427 = 2 ft³.

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 12-centimeter edges. How many cubes fill the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 2 12 ÷ 12 = 5, 1 ÷ 12 = 2, 1 ÷ 12 = 2 cubes. 5 × 2 × 2 = 20 cubes. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: A cube with 1-unit edges is cut into small cubes. Each small cube has edges of 12 unit. What is the volume of one small cube?
items.e: 8 small cubes fill 1 cubic unit, so each one is 18 cubic unit. The formula agrees: 12 × 12 × 12 = 18.

items.q: How many cubes with 14-centimeter edges fill a cube with 1-centimeter edges?
items.e: 4 small cubes fit along each edge: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. (16 is only one layer.)

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 12-foot edges. How many cubes fill the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 2 ÷ 12 = 4, 1 ÷ 12 = 2, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3 cubes. 4 × 2 × 3 = 24 cubes. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: A small cube has edges that are 14 inch long. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 14 × 14 × 14 = 164 in³. Multiply the edge by itself 3 times, not by 3 (3 × 14 = 34).

items.q: A cube with 1-unit edges is cut into small cubes with edges of 13 unit. What is the volume of one small cube?
items.e: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 small cubes fill 1 cubic unit, so each is 127 cubic unit: 13 × 13 × 13 = 127. (Adding 13 + 13 + 13 = 1 is not volume.)

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 12-inch edges. How many cubes fill the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 2 ÷ 12 = 4, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3 cubes. 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 cubes. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: The box is packed with cubes that have 12-centimeter edges. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Along the edges: 2 12 ÷ 12 = 5, 1 12 ÷ 12 = 3, 1 ÷ 12 = 2 cubes. 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubes. Each cube is 18 cm³, so V = 30 × 18 = 3 34 cm³. Check: 2 12 × 1 12 × 1 = 3 34.

items.q: A box is packed with 96 cubes that have 14-centimeter edges, with no gaps. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: One cube is 14 × 14 × 14 = 164 cm³. 96 cubes: 96 × 164 = 9664 = 1 12 cm³.

items.q: How many cubes with 12-inch edges fill a box that is 2 in long, 1 in wide and 1 12 in tall?
items.e: Along the edges: 4, 2 and 3 cubes (2 cubes for each inch). 4 × 2 × 3 = 24 cubes. Check: V = 3 in³, and each cube is 18 in³: 3 × 8 = 24.

sets.title: Use V = l × w × h with fractions

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 × 6 × 14 = 244 = 6 in³.

items.q: A box is 2 14 ft long, 1 12 ft wide and 3 ft tall. Which expression gives its volume?
c: 2 14 × 1 12 × 3
2 14 × 1 12
2 14 + 1 12 + 3
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 2 14 × 1 12 × 3 = 10 18 ft³. Keep the fraction parts: using only the whole numbers changes the edges.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 1 12 in long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge is the same, so V = 1 12 × 1 12 × 1 12 = 32 × 32 × 32 = 278 = 3 38 in³.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 4 12 cm long, 23 cm wide and 6 cm tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 12 × 23 × 6 = 92 × 23 × 6 = 1086 = 18 cm³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 14 × 3 12 × 1 12 = 174 × 72 × 32 = 35716 = 22 516 ft³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 3 13 × 2 × 7 = 103 × 2 × 7 = 1403 = 46 23 in³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 2 12 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge is the same, so V = 2 12 × 2 12 × 2 12 = 52 × 52 × 52 = 1258 = 15 58 cm³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 1 12 × 23 × 3 = 32 × 23 × 3 = 186 = 3 cm³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 5 in long, 1 13 in wide and 2 14 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 5 × 1 13 × 2 14 = 5 × 43 × 94 = 18012 = 15 in³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 2 × 2 34 × 2 12 = 2 × 114 × 52 = 1108 = 13 34 m³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 1 13 × 2 23 × 5 = 43 × 83 × 5 = 1609 = 17 79 ft³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 34 × 5 = 904 = 22 12 cm³.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 6 14 in long, 2 25 in wide and 1 12 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 14 × 2 25 × 1 12 = 254 × 125 × 32 = 90040 = 22 12 in³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 2 12 × 2 × 3 13 = 52 × 2 × 103 = 1006 = 16 23 m³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 3 12 ft long, 2 ft wide and 34 ft tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 3 12 × 2 × 34 = 72 × 2 × 34 = 428 = 5 14 ft³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 3 12 × 1 23 × 3 = 72 × 53 × 3 = 1056 = 17 12 ft³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 23 m long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge is the same, so V = 23 × 23 × 23 = 827 m³.

items.q: A box is 3 12 in long, 2 in wide and 12 in tall. Which expression gives its volume?
c: 3 12 + 2 + 12
3 12 × 2 × 12
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 3 12 × 2 × 12 = 3 12 in³. Keep the fraction parts: using only the whole numbers changes the edges.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 2 34 m long, 1 12 m wide and 4 m tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 2 34 × 1 12 × 4 = 114 × 32 × 4 = 1328 = 16 12 m³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 12 × 3 × 4 = 92 × 3 × 4 = 1082 = 54 in³. Change mixed numbers to fractions before you multiply.

items.q: A box is filled with cubes that have 12-inch edges. Each layer has 12 cubes, and there are 5 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Cubes: 12 × 5 = 60. Each cube is 18 in³, so V = 60 × 18 = 7 12 in³. (B × h works too: B = 12 × 14 in², h = 5 × 12 in.)

items.q: A box is filled with cubes that have 13-foot edges. Each layer has 18 cubes, and there are 4 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Cubes: 18 × 4 = 72. Each cube is 127 ft³, so V = 72 × 127 = 2 23 ft³. (B × h works too: B = 18 × 19 ft², h = 4 × 13 ft.)

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: V = B × h = 6 23 × 34 = 203 × 34 = 6012 = 5 m³. B is already length × width, so multiply it by the height only.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 14 ft². The prism is 3 34 ft tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 14 × 3 34 = 14 × 154 = 2104 = 52 12 ft³.

items.q: A prism has a base that is 2 12 ft long and 2 ft wide. It is 1 12 ft tall. What is B, the area of the base?
items.e: B = length × width = 2 12 × 2 = 5 ft². The height is not part of the base.

items.q: A prism has a base that is 6 m long and 1 13 m wide. It is 2 12 m tall. Use B × h to find its volume.
items.e: B = 6 × 1 13 = 8 m². V = B × h = 8 × 2 12 = 8 × 52 = 402 = 20 m³.

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: V = B × h = 10 12 × 2 13 = 212 × 73 = 1476 = 24 12 in³. B is already length × width, so multiply it by the height only.

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: V = B × h = 12 × 1 14 = 12 × 54 = 604 = 15 ft³. B is already length × width, so multiply it by the height only.

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: V = B × h = 2 14 × 4 = 94 × 4 = 364 = 9 cm³. B is already length × width, so multiply it by the height only.

items.q: A prism has a base that is 3 12 cm long and 1 12 cm wide. It is 2 cm tall. Use B × h to find its volume.
items.e: B = 3 12 × 1 12 = 5 14 cm². V = B × h = 5 14 × 2 = 214 × 2 = 424 = 10 12 cm³.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 6 34 ft². The prism is 2 ft tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 6 34 × 2 = 274 × 2 = 544 = 13 12 ft³.

items.q: A box is filled with cubes that have 12-centimeter edges. Each layer has 20 cubes, and there are 3 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Cubes: 20 × 3 = 60. Each cube is 18 cm³, so V = 60 × 18 = 7 12 cm³. (B × h works too: B = 20 × 14 cm², h = 3 × 12 cm.)

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: V = B × h = 7 12 × 1 12 = 152 × 32 = 454 = 11 14 in³. B is already length × width, so multiply it by the height only.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 6 in². The prism is 2 12 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 6 × 2 12 = 6 × 52 = 302 = 15 in³.

items.q: A prism has a base that is 4 in long and 2 14 in wide. It is 23 in tall. What is B, the area of the base?
items.e: B = length × width = 4 × 2 14 = 9 in². The height is not part of the base.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 17 12 in². The prism is 1 13 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 17 12 × 1 13 = 352 × 43 = 1406 = 23 13 in³.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 5 13 m². The prism is 2 14 m tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 5 13 × 2 14 = 163 × 94 = 14412 = 12 m³.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 10 cm². The prism is 35 cm tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 10 × 35 = 305 = 6 cm³.

items.q: A box is filled with cubes that have 12-inch edges. Each layer has 24 cubes, and there are 6 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Cubes: 24 × 6 = 144. Each cube is 18 in³, so V = 144 × 18 = 18 in³. (B × h works too: B = 24 × 14 in², h = 6 × 12 in.)

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: V = B × h = 18 × 56 = 906 = 15 ft³. B is already length × width, so multiply it by the height only.

items.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of 15 cm³. It is 8 cm long and 34 cm wide. How tall is it?
items.e: 8 × 34 = 6, so 6 × ? = 15. ? = 15 ÷ 6 = 15 × 16 = 156 = 2 12 cm. Check: 8 × 34 × 2 12 = 15.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 0.5 m long, 0.4 m wide and 3 m tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 0.5 × 0.4 × 3 = 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 m³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 20 in³. The area of its base is 7 12 in². What is its height?
items.e: V = B × h, so 7 12 × h = 20. h = 20 ÷ 7 12 = 20 × 215 = 4015 = 2 23 in.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 12 in long, 4.5 in wide and 2 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 12 × 4.5 × 2 = 54 × 2 = 108 in³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of 11 14 in³. It is 6 in long and 1 12 in wide. How tall is it?
items.e: 6 × 1 12 = 9, so 9 × ? = 11 14. ? = 11 14 ÷ 9 = 454 × 19 = 4536 = 1 14 in. Check: 6 × 1 12 × 1 14 = 11 14.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 4.2 in long, 2.5 in wide and 3 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 4.2 × 2.5 × 3 = 10.5 × 3 = 31.5 in³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: The volume of this prism is 15 m³. What is the length of the edge marked ?
items.e: 2 × 1 23 = 3 13, so 3 13 × ? = 15. ? = 15 ÷ 3 13 = 15 × 310 = 4510 = 4 12 m. Check: 4 12 × 2 × 1 23 = 15.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 11 23 cm³. The area of its base is 14 cm². What is its height?
items.e: V = B × h, so 14 × h = 11 23. h = 11 23 ÷ 14 = 353 × 114 = 3542 = 56 cm.

items.q: The volume of this prism is 5 58 ft³. What is the length of the edge marked ?
items.e: 2 12 × 1 12 = 3 34, so 3 34 × ? = 5 58. ? = 5 58 ÷ 3 34 = 458 × 415 = 180120 = 1 12 ft. Check: 2 12 × 1 12 × 1 12 = 5 58.

items.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of 18 m³. It is 2.5 m long and 1.2 m wide. How tall is it?
The volume of this prism is 14 cm³. What is the length of the edge marked ?
items.e: 3 × 3 12 = 10 12, so 10 12 × ? = 14. ? = 14 ÷ 10 12 = 14 × 221 = 2821 = 1 13 cm. Check: 3 × 1 13 × 3 12 = 14.

items.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of 15 in³. It is 3 in wide and 1 12 in tall. How long is it?
items.e: 3 × 1 12 = 4 12, so 4 12 × ? = 15. ? = 15 ÷ 4 12 = 15 × 29 = 309 = 3 13 in. Check: 3 13 × 3 × 1 12 = 15.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 11 14 ft³. The area of its base is 4 12 ft². What is its height?
items.e: V = B × h, so 4 12 × h = 11 14. h = 11 14 ÷ 4 12 = 454 × 29 = 9036 = 2 12 ft.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 15 58 ft³. How long is each edge?
items.e: All 3 edges of a cube are equal. Find a number you multiply 3 times to get 1258: 52 × 52 × 52 = 1258. Each edge is 2 12 ft.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 3 38 in³. How long is each edge?
items.e: All 3 edges of a cube are equal. Find a number you multiply 3 times to get 278: 32 × 32 × 32 = 278. Each edge is 1 12 in.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 6 cm long, 2.5 cm wide and 0.8 cm tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 6 × 2.5 × 0.8 = 15 × 0.8 = 12 cm³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of 17 12 ft³. It is 3 12 ft long and 2 ft tall. How wide is it?
items.e: 3 12 × 2 = 7, so 7 × ? = 17 12. ? = 17 12 ÷ 7 = 352 × 17 = 3514 = 2 12 ft. Check: 3 12 × 2 12 × 2 = 17 12.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 2.5 m long, 1.2 m wide and 4 m tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 2.5 × 1.2 × 4 = 3 × 4 = 12 m³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: The volume of this prism is 7 12 in³. What is the length of the edge marked ?
items.e: 4 × 2 12 = 10, so 10 × ? = 7 12. ? = 7 12 ÷ 10 = 152 × 110 = 1520 = 34 in. Check: 4 × 2 12 × 34 = 7 12.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 1.5 ft long, 3 ft wide and 2.4 ft tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 1.5 × 3 × 2.4 = 4.5 × 2.4 = 10.8 ft³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: The bottom of a shoebox has an area of 72 in². The box is 4 12 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h = 72 × 4 12 = 72 × 92 = 6482 = 324 in³. (288 drops the 12.)

items.q: A moving box has a volume of 5 58 ft³. Its base is 2 12 ft long and 1 12 ft wide. How tall is it?
items.e: B = 2 12 × 1 12 = 3 34 ft². h = 5 58 ÷ 3 34 = 458 × 415 = 180120 = 1 12 ft.

items.q: Sofia keeps her cards in a cube-shaped box with 4 12-inch edges. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 4 12 × 4 12 × 4 12 = 92 × 92 × 92 = 7298 = 91 18 in³.

items.q: An aquarium is 40 cm long and 25 cm wide. The water in it is 20.5 cm deep. What is the volume of the water?
items.e: V = 40 × 25 × 20.5 = 1,000 × 20.5 = 20,500 cm³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: A raised garden bed is 8 13 ft long, 3 ft wide and 1 14 ft deep. How much soil fills it?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 8 13 × 3 × 1 14 = 253 × 3 × 54 = 37512 = 31 14 ft³.

items.q: A cereal box is 7 12 in wide, 2 12 in deep and 11 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 7 12 × 2 12 × 11 = 152 × 52 × 11 = 8254 = 206 14 in³.

items.q: Omar cuts a block of cheese that is 4 in long, 2 12 in wide and 1 12 in tall into cubes with 12-inch edges. How many cubes does he get?
items.e: Along the edges: 8, 5 and 3 cubes. 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 cubes. Check: V = 4 × 2 12 × 1 12 = 15 in³, and 15 × 8 = 120.

items.q: A wading pool is 10 m long and 4.5 m wide. The water is 1.2 m deep. How much water is in the pool?
items.e: V = 10 × 4.5 × 1.2 = 45 × 1.2 = 54 m³. Count the decimal places to place the point.

items.q: Nora has 30 ft³ of sand for a sandbox that is 6 ft long and 4 ft wide. How deep will the sand be?
items.e: B = 6 × 4 = 24 ft². 24 × h = 30, so h = 30 ÷ 24 = 3024 = 1 14 ft.

items.q: Lily's fish tank is 2 12 ft long, 1 ft wide and 1 12 ft tall. What is the volume of the tank?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 2 12 × 1 × 1 12 = 52 × 1 × 32 = 154 = 3 34 ft³.

items.q: Eli fills a gift box that is 3 in long, 2 in wide and 1 12 in tall with cubes that have 12-inch edges. How many cubes fit?
items.e: Along the edges: 6, 4 and 3 cubes (2 for each inch). 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubes. Check: V = 3 × 2 × 1 12 = 9 in³, and 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: A jewelry box is 2 in long, 1 12 in wide and 1 in tall. How many cubes with 14-inch edges fill it?
items.e: 4 cubes fit along each inch. Along the edges: 8, 6 and 4 cubes. 8 × 6 × 4 = 192. Check: V = 3 in³, and each cube is 164 in³: 3 × 64 = 192.

items.q: Box A is 3 in by 2 12 in by 2 in. Box B is a cube with 2 12-inch edges. Which box has the greater volume, and by how much?
c: A, by 58 in³
A, by 3 78 in³
B, by 58 in³
items.e: A: 3 × 2 12 × 2 = 15 in³. B: 52 × 52 × 52 = 1258 = 15 58 in³. 15 58 − 15 = 58, so B is greater by 58 in³. (Adding the edges gives 7 12 for both, but that is not volume.)

items.q: A box holds 120 sugar cubes with no gaps. Each sugar cube has 12-inch edges. What is the volume of the sugar?
items.e: One sugar cube is 18 in³. 120 × 18 = 1208 = 15 in³. (60 forgets that each cube is 18, not 12.)

items.q: A tank is 3 ft long, 1 12 ft wide and 2 ft tall. Water fills it to a depth of 1 14 ft. What is the volume of the water?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 3 × 1 12 × 1 14 = 3 × 32 × 54 = 458 = 5 58 ft³. (9 ft³ is the whole tank.)

items.q: A moving company charges for the space a load takes up in a truck. Which unit fits that measure best?
items.e: Space inside is volume, so it is measured in cubic units like ft³. Square feet measure area, feet measure length, and pounds measure weight.

items.q: Ruby stacks 10 hay bales. Each bale is 3 ft long, 1 12 ft wide and 1 13 ft tall. What is the total volume of the bales?
items.e: One bale: 3 × 1 12 × 1 13 = 3 × 32 × 43 = 6 ft³. Ten bales: 10 × 6 = 60 ft³.

items.q: The inside of a refrigerator is 2 12 ft wide, 2 ft deep and 5 12 ft tall. How much space is inside?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 2 12 × 2 × 5 12 = 52 × 2 × 112 = 1104 = 27 12 ft³.

items.q: Kai fills a sandbox that is 6 ft long and 4 12 ft wide with sand 34 ft deep. How many cubic feet of sand does he need?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 4 12 × 34 = 6 × 92 × 34 = 1628 = 20 14 ft³. The depth of the sand is the height.

items.q: A brick is 7 12 in long, 3 12 in wide and 2 14 in tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 7 12 × 3 12 × 2 14 = 152 × 72 × 94 = 94516 = 59 116 in³.
